procedure_cards.title: Use the repository-declared workspace toolchain
applies_when: The change touches a multi-package repository or a CLI with a root manifest.
counterexamples: A single-file script with no manifest or workspace boundary.
procedure: Read the root package.json, pyproject.toml, go.mod, or Cargo.toml first.
Use the package manager, workspace filter, and scripts named there before inventing a local command.
Limit edits and checks to the package boundary named by the manifest.
verification: Record the manifest path and run the smallest declared check covering the changed package.
recovery: If the manifest and directory layout disagree, stop moving files and ask which source is authoritative.

procedure_cards.title: Stage release records with the project source files
applies_when: A change will be packaged, tagged, or published in a project with a changelog or release-note source.
counterexamples: A local code experiment with no release or package action.
procedure: Read the changelog or release-note format before preparing a version.
Add the release record through the project’s documented source format, such as a changelog section or fragment.
Run the declared checks and review the generated or staged diff before any publish step.
verification: Confirm the staged release text names the changed package and matches the target commit.
recovery: If an immutable artifact was published before the tag or release completed, inventory package, tag, and release state before retrying.

procedure_cards.title: Route broad feature work through triage or RFCs
applies_when: A proposed feature is broad, user-facing, or likely to affect several packages.
counterexamples: A narrowly scoped typo or an already assigned maintenance fix.
procedure: Read the contribution guide for issue labels, roadmap priorities, RFCs, and required test plans.
Search existing issues and proposals before implementation.
Open or link the project’s canonical discussion record before coding when the guide requires prior design.
verification: Ensure the pull request links the issue or RFC and includes the contribution guide’s requested checks.
recovery: If the idea is outside the current roadmap or lacks an owner, stop implementation and request maintainer direction.

procedure_cards.title: Use the documented private security channel
applies_when: A report may expose an exploitable vulnerability, credential, or sensitive reproduction.
counterexamples: A normal bug clearly outside the project’s security policy.
procedure: Read SECURITY.md or the security section of the project documentation.
Send vulnerability details through the private channel named by the project.
Keep exploit details and credentials out of public issues and pull requests.
verification: Record the policy URL and acknowledgement or escalation path without claiming that a fix has shipped.
recovery: If sensitive details were posted publicly, stop repeating them, follow the project’s escalation path, and rotate exposed credentials.
